name: Security Layer
description: Defines how the system identifies, authorizes and protects: authentication configuration, roles, permissions, secure resources and their operations, access conditions and field-level controls, declarative policies and rules, data classification and rate limits, together with goal-oriented security concepts such as actors, objectives, delegations, threats, countermeasures and accountability (NIST SP 800-53 controls with STS-ml and XACML-style policy modelling). Code that checks identity or enforces permissions is evidence for elements here. Modelling rules: the security model composes its authentication configuration, constraints container and policies, and aggregates the shared elements (actors, roles, permissions, secure resources, information entities, delegations, threats, classifications and accountability requirements); a policy composes its rules, and a secure resource composes its operations and field access controls. Actors are assigned to roles, roles aggregate permissions and specialize a parent role, and permissions authorize resource operations; access follows that chain. An authentication configuration authenticates actors, uses its password policy and protects resources. A policy rule uses the conditions it evaluates, protects its target, authorizes permissions, triggers its policy actions and generates evidence; conditions and actions do not constrain or trigger on their own. Policies (security, password, retention and data classification) mandate the countermeasures they call for, and only countermeasures mitigate threats. A threat targets resources, information entities and business processes and services, influences classifications and policies, and references the motivation driver it gives rise to. Audit configurations, policy rules and delegations generate evidence; an audit configuration monitors resources and satisfies accountability requirements, and a retention policy governs the audit trails, evidence and information it keeps. A data classification governs the information entities, secure resources and retention policies it labels; field access controls are constrained by it, and data elements in other layers reference it. Separation of duty, binding of duty and need to know constrain roles, permissions and operations; the constraints container only groups them, and other layers link to the individual rule they follow. Validation rules constrain field values; they do not decide access.
